ask.text: Ask the user a structured question and wait for the answer. Use it only when the decision genuinely belongs to the user (an irreversible choice, a preference with no defensible default) or when you are blocked on information only they have; do not ask things you can find out with the other tools. Send 1-5 questions, each with 2-6 options; mark the obvious default as recommended. Without an interactive UI the call returns a note telling you to proceed with the most conservative option instead of blocking.

bash.text: Run a shell command. stdout and stderr are merged; output is truncated to head+tail if very large. Runs non-interactively (pagers/prompts are disabled) and in an optional cwd. Report the exit code yourself when it matters. With async=true the command runs in the background and the wait tool collects its result.

edit_file.text: Replace an exact string in a file. By default old_string must match exactly once; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. On zero matches (or multiple matches without replace_all) the file is left unchanged. The file's CRLF line endings and BOM are kept.

fetch.text: Fetch a URL and return its readable text (HTML stripped). Use it after `web_search` to read a result in full.

glob.text: Find files by glob pattern (e.g. '**/*.py') under a directory. Hidden files are skipped unless include_hidden, and paths ignored by the root .gitignore are skipped unless include_ignored; returns at most limit paths (default 500). sort='path' (default) or 'mtime' (newest first).

grep.text: Search file contents with a regular expression. Uses ripgrep when available, otherwise a slow Python scan. Results are grouped by file and paged: at most 20 matching files and 20 hits per file per call. A truncated page reports the skip value for the next page.

list_dir.text: List one directory level, marking directories and file sizes.

read_file.text: Read a UTF-8 text file. Binary files are refused. Returns whole small files; at most 1000 lines per call by default (hard cap 5000). A truncated result reports the exact offset for the next page. Set line_numbers=true to prefix each line with its 1-based number (for inspection only; never write numbered text back).

read_skill.text: Load a skill's instructions by name before following it. Available skills: alpha, beta

task.text: Delegate a self-contained job to a subagent that returns only a final report. Its tools mirror this session's permission mode (read-only outside zen). async: true returns a task id at once — collect later with wait; model picks the child's model (id or provider/id). Before dispatch: confirm every file you reference exists; precompute what the child lacks (write the diff to a file); parallel workers must not share files; state the output contract. After collecting workers, re-run the full test suite yourself before continuing.

todo.text: Track progress on a multi-step task with a phased checklist. Use it when the work has 3+ steps, call it in the same response as your plan, and keep it current: start a task before working on it, mark it done when it is (or drop it), and block it with a one-line reason when you cannot proceed. Tasks are addressed by their exact content, never by generated IDs. Phases run in order and the in-progress pointer advances automatically. One op per call: init replaces the list; start/done/drop/block/unblock take a task (done/drop/block/unblock also accept a phase, and default to every task); rm removes a task or clears a phase; append adds tasks to a phase; view is a read-only checklist. A failed call changes nothing.

wait.text: Wait for a background job and return its result. job_id accepts bash job ids (bg_N, from bash async: true) and task ids (task_N, from task async: true — the child's full report envelope). Without job_id it waits for any running bash job. On timeout it returns a still-running snapshot, so call wait again for the result.

web_search.text:
Search the web: returns titles, URLs and snippets. Use it when the answer depends on information outside this repository (current library APIs, release notes, error messages).
The query accepts Google-style operators: "exact phrase", -exclude, site:domain, -site:domain, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, inurl:word, lang:en, after:2025-01-01, before:2026-01-01, and `a OR b`. Each engine gets only the operators it understands; constraints that would return nothing are relaxed and reported.
Chain: DeepSeek -> Tavily -> Brave -> Bing -> DuckDuckGo, first usable wins. Returns at most 8 results; follow up with `fetch` to read a page.

write_file.text: Write UTF-8 text to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the whole file. An existing file's CRLF line endings and UTF-8 BOM are kept; a new file is written with LF line endings.
